Thanks — quick read below and recommended approach:

- Subprocessor notification: Accept 30 days notice for non-critical additions. For security-critical patches or mitigations we will allow immediate onboarding with post-notification; will document the exception in the DPA.
- Objection window: Standard commercial ask is 10 business days. For faster closes we can offer 7 business days if Acme signs an amendment to the DPA committing to expedited review. Recommend we start with 10 business days to match their preference.
- Transfers: We support SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) and can sign equivalent safeguards; include a clause referencing SCCs and backlog to support EU->US transfers.
- KMS/HSM: We do not offer customer-managed HSM in hosted mode by default. We can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted we can document encryption-at-rest plus customer-specific key support via KMS integrations for Dedicated.

I attached a redline (Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf) and the current subprocessor list (Subprocessor_List_2026-02-24.csv). My suggested position is: accept 30-day subprocessor notice + 10-business-day objection window; confirm SCCs and note KMS limitation with DPA appendix pointing to Dedicated/Private options.

If that works I recommend we send the redlined DPA back via DocuSign envelope and offer a 30-day notification schedule in the DPA with the security exception language.

-Rishi

- Objection process: 10 business days to notify Redwood of a material objection. If an objection is timely raised, Redwood and Acme will meet in good faith to resolve; if unresolved, Acme may request mitigation measures or escalating remedies as laid out in Section 6.
